text:
aj: heads-up — proposing a weekend capacity sweep to move low-priority batch jobs into preemptible/spot pools overnight to cut GPU spend. thinking 00:00-07:00 UTC window, mixed-capacity pools with on-demand fallback. thoughts? :wave:

devon: sounds reasonable. couple of constraints: we need checkpointing + a retry budget per job, and an explicit backfill window so interactive jobs don't starve. also prefer prioritized queues rather than ad-hoc tagging.

maria: +1. two immediate q's: 1) interactive SLOs during the window? we can't risk slowdowns for latency-sensitive routes. 2) region constraints — eu-west has flaky preemptible churn during maintenance windows. might want region-aware scheduling. :thinking:

aj: interactive SLOs unchanged — we keep a baseline of on-demand capacity sized for P95 latency (<100ms for short prompts). batch jobs must be labeled `priority:low` and `preemptible_ok: true`. scheduler will only migrate those. sample queue config below:

aj: ```yaml
queues:
  - name: batch-low
    priority: 10
    allowed_types: [a10g, a100, gtx]
    preemptible: true
    checkpoint_interval_minutes: 20
    retry_budget: 2
    fallback_to_on_demand: true

  - name: interactive
    priority: 100
    preemptible: false
    min_on_demand: 6
```

kevin: FYI — persistent local SSDs on GCP preemptible VMs are lost on reclaim. plan to rely on object storage for checkpoints (s3/gcs) or a managed PV layer (NFS/EFS). also saw recently that ap-south and eu-west have slightly higher preemption rates when hypervisor maintenance kicks in. small log snippet from last week: `2026-02-09T03:12:14Z WARN gpu-allocator: preempted instance nvidia-a100-01 (spot)` — we lost ~18 tasks during a 10m window. link to dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/spot-interrupts (private)

devon: i ran a simple sim across historical preemption signals — rough results:

  - business-hours (eu-west): 7-day avg interruption probability ~15%
  - weekend-night (00:00-07:00 UTC): ~30% churn but much cheaper capacity
  - fallback->on-demand expected to absorb ~5% of peak needing immediate resources

so we need to tune retry_budget and checkpoint granularity. checkpoint every 15-20m seems like a good tradeoff for our batch jobs.

maria: proposal:
  - schedule window 00:00-07:00 UTC for preemptible-first placement
  - require `checkpoint_interval <= 30m` and `retry_budget >= 2` for moved jobs
  - use mixed-capacity pools (prefer cheapest compatible instance types) with explicit region weights (avoid ap-south majority)
  - assign queue priorities: interactive > standard > batch-low; batch-low gets lower preemption SLA but allowed to backfill heavily overnight

aj: rollout plan idea: canary on a tiny pool Friday night (15 GPUs) with 10 test jobs, monitor four KPIs for the first 3 hours: cost per GPU-hour, job failure rate, queue wait latency, and preemptive interrupt rate. abort if failure_rate > 3% or interrupt_rate causes >10% cost increase via fallbacks. who can own the canary?

devon: i'll own the canary. i'll add feature flags and a dry-run mode that simulates move decisions without actually migrating containers (so we can spot scheduling surprises).

kevin: i'll prep infra — PV checklist, IAM for checkpoint uploads, and a quick driver update on the canary nodes (older drivers correlate to higher JVM OOMs with preemptions).

aj: also updating alerts/billing: if expected cost delta > 15% savings, cool; but we must add a billing alarm if fallback-on-demand usage > 8% for 30m. devon, can you add that to the canary dashboard?

devon: done, added panels + alert.

aj: @sre-bot — please create a healthcheck that pages oncall if `preemptive_interrupt_rate > 5%` sustained for 5m during canary window.

sre-bot: created alert rule `preemptive_interrupt_rate_high_canary` -> pages oncall.

maria: small ops note — we should communicate to data-science teams about potential longer queue times and bump expected job durations in their notebooks. i'll draft a short blurb for #customer-success and #general.

aj: thanks all — i'll open the docs PR with the runbook + scheduler config and set the canary for 2026-03-20T23:00:00Z. TL;DR: move low-priority batch to preemptible overnight with checkpoints, mixed pools, on-demand fallback, and a guarded canary. :thumbsup:
